depiction.primary_object: central dot surrounded by two open concentric circular arcs
modifiers: exclamation mark on the bottom right

readings.meaning: wireless hotspot or radio broadcast issue / error

ambiguity: Closely resembles an Apple AirDrop or generic podcast icon; at small sizes, the concentric rings can look like a target, eye, or generic Wi-Fi symbol.
task_intents: fix broken internet or Wi-Fi signal
diagnose Bluetooth beacon or AirDrop failure
replace battery in offline motion sensor

example_tasks.task: Call T-Mobile about roaming hotspot not working on laptop
Figure out why the garage door sensor keeps throwing alerts
Move mesh router node closer to the kitchen to stop dropouts
Debug BLE beacon signal loss in the warehouse tracking app
Check why the baby monitor loses signal after midnight
Fix OBS stream dropping frames when broadcasting on 5GHz
Reboot the ubiquiti access point in the third-floor hallway
Find out why guest Wi-Fi shows connected with no internet on Android phones
Update firmware on the backyard weather station sensor before it disconnects again
Ask IT to check the conference room wireless presentation dongle before Tuesday's pitch

example_tasks_es: Reiniciar el repetidor Wi-Fi del pasillo que está en rojo
Llamar a Movistar por los cortes de señal en el estudio

reasoning: The icon depicts a wireless broadcast/hotspot symbol (central node with radiating concentric arcs) paired with an exclamation mark indicating an alert or failure. It fits tasks centered on troubleshooting Wi-Fi, hotspot, beacon, or smart-sensor connection problems, though it can be confused with a normal hotspot, podcast, or target glyph if the exclamation mark is overlooked.
